reason: Abstract states the authors conducted 'a replication of Mintzberg's study' on whether managers plan, re-testing his observational finding with new data.
This evaluates the ICH-score's predictive validity in a new patient population, which is instrument validation, not replication of a specific finding.
Prior CBF findings are mentioned as background/rationale for a new diagnostic-biomarker proof-of-concept study, and it's not clear re-testing that finding is the study's aim.

This is a scientific rebuttal about gene recombination artifacts; 'replication' appears only in the biological/technical sense (plasmid replication of an approach), not as a study re-testing a published finding.
The study develops a new VR/haptic paradigm to 'reproduce the effect' of prism adaptation as a methodological innovation, not to re-test a specific prior finding.
'Replication' refers to enterovirus genome replication (a biological process), unrelated to replicating a published finding.
The two studies replicate one another within the same paper to validate use-case quality metrics, not re-test a prior published finding, and metric validation is explicitly excluded.
The study evaluates/confirms the reproducibility of a surgical graft-preparation procedure, which is procedure validation, not replication of a published finding.
The 'replication' referenced is an internal re-analysis of the dissertation's own first research question's combinations across subgroups, not a re-test of an externally published finding.
The study characterizes measurement reproducibility of an MRI technique and only briefly notes results are consistent with ('replicating') prior HD literature in passing, not as a study aim.
This validates the diagnostic 'Ogata score' instrument's performance in a new regional population, which is instrument validation, explicitly excluded.
